newsitem.title: UK: Brazil's Unibanco plans $300 mln bond.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Unibanco plans $300 mln bond.

text.p: Uniao de Bancos Brasileiros SA (Unibanco) is expected to launch a two-tranche bond for a total $300 million this week, bankers said on Monday.
Morgan Stanley is lead manager of the transaction for the Brazilian retail bank, expected to be launched on Tuesday.
A $200 million tranche will have a three-year maturity and a $100 million tranche will have a six-year maturity, bankers said.
Price talk for the three-year tranche is 160-170 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, dealers said.
Price talk for the six-year tranche is 200-220 b.p. over.
Unibanco last tapped the dollar sector in June, with a $150 million three-year bond priced to yield 150 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
In May, Moody's Investors Service raised Unibanco's financial strength rating to C+ from C.
Moody's also confirmed Unibanco's long term foreign currency rating of B2, noting that the bank's debt ratings were constrained by the sovereign ceiling set by Moody's for Brazilian risk.
